info.name: Stock Portfolio Backend
info.description:
All 11 endpoints of the stock_portfolio_be server (Express 5 + Prisma 7 + PostgreSQL).

**How to use**
1. Set `baseUrl` in the collection variables (default `http://localhost:5001`).
2. Run **Auth → Register** or **Auth → Login**. The test script saves the JWT into the `token` variable, and every other request sends it as `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` automatically.
3. Run **Broker accounts → Link broker account**. The test script saves `brokerAccountId` and `portfolioId` for the requests that need them.
4. Run **Sync trades** within 15 minutes of linking (the broker session lives in memory and expires).

Full documentation: `docs/API_DOCUMENTATION.md`.

item.name: Auth
item.description: No token needed. Both requests return a JWT that the test script stores in `{{token}}`.

request.description:
Creates a user and returns a login token.

**Responses**
- `201` `{ message: "success", data: { id, fullName }, token }`
- `400` `{ message: "user already exists" }`
- `500` HTML page if a required field is missing (no validation yet).

Logs in and returns a JWT (valid 7 days by default).

**Responses**
- `200` `{ status: "success", data: { user: { id, fullName, email }, token } }`
- `401` `{ message: "Invalid email or passowrd" }` — same message for unknown email and wrong password.

item.name: Broker accounts
item.description: Needs `{{token}}`. Link an AHL eTrade account, list, disconnect, and sync trades.

request.description:
Logs in to the AHL eTrade website with the broker credentials, creates (or re-activates) the `broker_accounts` row and its portfolio (`AHL <accountNumber>`), and keeps the broker cookies in server memory for **15 minutes**. The broker password is never stored.

The test script saves `brokerAccountId` and `portfolioId` into collection variables.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { brokerAccountId, portfolioId, status, sessionCookie, cookies, enabledDigits } }`
- `400` `{ error: "accountNumber and password are required." }`
- `400` `{ error: "Password is too short: the broker asked for character N." }`
- `401` `{ error: "Invalid broker credentials." }`
- `502` `{ error: "No session cookie was returned by the broker login page." }`
- `502` `{ error: "No enabled Digit fields were found in the broker login page." }`

Lists the caller's linked broker accounts, newest first, each with its portfolio.

`syncStatus` is `idle` or `disconnected`; `lastSyncedAt` is `null` until the first sync.

If `brokerAccountId` / `portfolioId` are still empty, the test script fills them from the first account.

exec: console.log('brokerAccountId + portfolioId filled from first account');

query.description: Passed to the broker: BUY, SELL or ALL (default ALL)
Passed to the broker: one symbol or ALL (default ALL)

request.description:
Downloads the broker's order history and current holdings, upserts securities and trades, recomputes positions (average-cost method, merged with the broker's holdings) and records today's price for each held stock.

Does **not** log in — it reuses the in-memory session from *Link broker account*. Run it within 15 minutes of linking, otherwise you get `401` and must link again. Safe to re-run: trades are not duplicated.

All query params are optional; enable them in the Params tab to override the defaults.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ message: "success", data: { securities, trades, positions, prices, fromCollaterals, fromTrades, mismatches[], from, to } }`
- `401` `{ error: "Broker session expired. Reconnect the account to continue." }`
- `404` `{ error: "account does not exist" }`

response.name: 401 Broker session expired
response.body: { "error": "Broker session expired. Reconnect the account to continue." }

request.description:
Unlinks the broker account: sets `syncStatus` to `disconnected`. Trades, positions and the portfolio are **kept**.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ message: "account disconnected successfully", data: { account: { id, clientCode, syncStatus } } }`
- `404` `{ error: "account does not exist" }` — not found or belongs to another user.

item.name: Portfolio
item.description: Needs `{{token}}`. Read-only views of the portfolio built by the sync.

request.description:
Lists the caller's portfolios. One portfolio is created automatically per linked broker account, named `AHL <clientCode>`, base currency `PKR`.

If `portfolioId` is still empty, the test script fills it from the first portfolio.

query.description: YYYY-MM-DD — enable together with `to` to get a `trend` array per position

request.description:
Current holdings with the latest known price and P&L, plus a summary. All numbers are real JSON numbers.

- `lastPrice` / `marketValue` / `unrealizedPnl` are `null` when no price is stored yet for that stock.
- `summary` totals cover **only priced positions**; `unpricedPositions` says how many were left out.
- A portfolio that is not yours returns an empty `positions` array (200, not 404).

**Trend:** every position carries `trend: [ { date, close }, … ]` (oldest first) for the window in `data.range`. The default window is the last 12 months ending today; enable both `from` and `to` in the Params tab to change it. A stock with no bars in the window gets `trend: []` but keeps its `lastPrice`.

**Which stocks:** only those held at some point inside the window (quantity above zero at `from`, or a BUY inside it). A stock bought after `to`, or fully sold before `from`, is left out; `summary` totals only the rows returned.

**400** when only one date is sent, a date is not `YYYY-MM-DD`, `from` is after `to`, or the window is wider than 5 years.

Trade history, newest first, with pagination.

Note: `quantity`, `price`, `commission` and `netAmount` come back as **strings** (Prisma Decimal) — convert with `Number()` on the client.

item.name: Market data
item.description: Needs `{{token}}`. Daily price history from the Arif Habib analytics API.

request.description:
Downloads ~5 years of daily OHLCV bars for the securities that matter — every stock currently **held**, every stock on a **watchlist**, and the `KSE100` benchmark — and inserts only the days not already stored. The other ~500 rows in `securities` exist for search and are never fetched.

A symbol whose newest bar is already today (Karachi date) is skipped without a request. Calls are spaced 400 ms apart, so ~20 symbols take about 8 seconds. Safe to re-run any time.

Needs a live broker session (`Link broker account` within the last 15 minutes) so the analytics hand-off can mint a market cookie.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { securities, fetched, skipped, newRows, results: [ { symbol, fetched, saved } | { symbol, skipped } | { symbol, error } ] } }`
- `401` `{ error: "Broker session expired. Reconnect the account so a market session can be issued." }`
- `404` `{ error: "account does not exist" }`

response.name: 401 No market session
response.body: { "error": "Broker session expired. Reconnect the account so a market session can be issued." }

query.description: YYYY-MM-DD — enable together with `to`; default window is the last 12 months

request.description:
Daily OHLCV bars for one symbol straight from the `daily_prices` table — no broker or market session needed. Change `KSE100` in the path to any stock symbol (case-insensitive).

Data is only as fresh as the last **Sync daily prices** run; `asOf` is the newest bar date returned.

- Default window: the last 12 months ending today. Enable both `from` and `to` in the Params tab to change it (max 5 years).
- Bars are oldest first. `open`/`high`/`low`/`volume` may be `null` on the close-only bar the broker sync writes.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ message: "success", data: { symbol, range, asOf, bars: [ { date, open, high, low, close, volume } ] } }`
- `400` bad `from`/`to` (same rules as Positions)
- `404` `{ error: "security does not exist" }`

One-time import of the broker's full symbol list (`GET /Home/GetSymolsList`). Fills `securities` with every **Approved**, non-futures symbol on the exchange (~557 rows) with real company names and sectors, so `Search securities` has something to find. Also upgrades the placeholder rows the trade sync created (name = symbol).

Safe to re-run — upserts by symbol. Needs a live broker session.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { received, saved } }` — raw rows received vs distinct symbols saved
- `401` `{ error: "Broker session expired. Reconnect the account." }`
- `404` `{ error: "account does not exist" }`

query.description: At least 2 characters. Matches symbol or company name, case-insensitive.

request.description:
Search `securities` by symbol or company name — the picker for adding to the watchlist. Database only; no broker session needed. Returns at most 20 rows.

Stocks you currently **hold** and stocks **already on your watchlist** are excluded, so the picker only offers things you can add. The same query therefore returns different rows for different users.

The test script saves the first result's `id` into the `securityId` collection variable, ready for `Add to watchlist`.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { securities: [ { id, symbol, companyName, sector } ] } }`
- `400` `{ error: "q must be at least 2 characters" }`

One stock against the `KSE100` benchmark over a period, **both rebased to 100 on the first day**, so they share one axis. The payload for the two-line comparison chart. Change `FFC` in the path to any symbol.

Only trading days both series have are returned, so the lines always align. If the stock listed after the window began the range is clamped — check `range.from`.

Chart `stock` and `benchmark`; show `close` in the tooltip; put `summary` in the header. `outperformance` = `stockReturn − benchmarkReturn` in percentage points.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { symbol, period, range, series: [ { date, close, stock, benchmark } ], summary: { stockReturn, benchmarkReturn, outperformance } } }`
- `400` `{ error: "period must be one of 1W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y" }`
- `404` `{ error: "security does not exist" }`
- `404` `{ error: "not enough price history for this period" }`

exec: if (data) console.log(`${data.symbol} ${data.period}: ${data.series.length} pts, stock ${data.summary.stockReturn.toFixed(2)}% vs KSE100 ${data.summary.benchmarkReturn.toFixed(2)}% -> ${data.summary.outperformance.toFixed(2)} pts`);

item.name: Watchlist
item.description: A per-user list of securities to follow. Find things to add with `Market data → Search securities` (which sets `securityId`). Watched symbols are included automatically in `Sync daily prices`.

request.description:
Your watchlist with the latest price and the day's change per item, plus the same for `KSE100` as a benchmark row to show on top. Comes from `daily_prices` (last two closes), so it is as fresh as the last price sync.

**Nulls to handle:** a symbol added since the last sync has no bars → `lastPrice`, `change`, `changePct`, `asOf` all `null`. One bar only → `change`/`changePct` null. Render "—", not 0.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ data: { benchmark: { securityId, symbol, companyName, sector, lastPrice, change, changePct, asOf }, items: [ …same shape… ] } }`

response.name: 200 OK

request.description:
Add a security to your watchlist. `securityId` is a `securities.id` — run `Search securities` first and it is set for you. Idempotent: adding the same one again returns `200` and changes nothing. No body.

If the stock has no price history yet and a market session is alive (you synced in the last ~2 h), its full history is fetched in this request so it shows a price immediately — `pricesLoaded: true`. Otherwise it is inserted anyway with `pricesLoaded: false` and the next **Sync daily prices** fills it.

**Responses**
- `200` `{ message: "success", data: { symbol, pricesLoaded } }`
- `404` `{ error: "security does not exist" }`

exec: if (data) console.log(`added ${data.symbol} — prices ${data.pricesLoaded ? 'loaded now' : 'will load on next sync'}`);

request.description:
Remove a security from your watchlist. Scoped to you — an id that is not on your list is a `404`.

Only the link row is deleted; the security and its price history stay in the database (they are shared, and re-adding needs no re-download).

**Responses**
- `200` `{ message: "success" }`
- `404` `{ error: "not in watchlist" }`
